title: ClusterKV: Manipulating LLM KV Cache in Semantic Space for Recallable Compression
problem: Long-context LLM inference (32K+ tokens) incurs massive KV cache memory costs and increased latency due to extensive memory accesses. Recent KV compression methods either permanently evict tokens (losing recall capability) or recall at coarse granularity (page/positional), degrading accuracy and output quality.
motivation: Context lengths are growing rapidly; KV cache is a critical memory and latency bottleneck; selective recall at fine granularity is needed for accuracy.
method: ClusterKV compresses the KV cache by grouping tokens that mean similar things (semantic clustering) and deciding which clusters to keep—rather than permanently erasing tokens or simply grouping by position in the text. When processing long contexts, it selectively recalls only the most relevant semantic clusters, shrinking the cache to a 1K–2K token budget even for 32K-token inputs. The system uses efficient algorithms for clustering tokens, selecting which ones matter, indexing them, and caching the results.
key_novelty: Compressing the KV cache by grouping tokens by meaning (semantic clustering) and selectively recalling clusters, rather than permanently deleting tokens or using position-based grouping.
contributions: Efficient clustering, selection, indexing algorithms for KV management
Negligible accuracy loss across tasks with 1K–2K KV cache for 32K contexts
Higher accuracy/output quality vs. SOTA recallable KV methods
limitations: Evaluation on specific LLM architectures (not detailed); generalization to encoder-decoder or vision-language models; clustering overhead not quantified; comparison with recent sparse attention methods not discussed.
primary_theme: semantic-cluster-based recallable KV cache compression for long-context LLM inference
